newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian police get cash for trapping actress.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian police get cash for trapping actress.

text.p: Five Indonesian police detectives have received cash rewards for capturing a fugitive actress who fled to the United States after being arrested for possessing some 30,000 Ecstasy pills, the Jakarta Post said on Tuesday.

The detectives were given between 400,000 rupiah ($168) and one million rupiah ($427.90) each for their work in locating the actress Zarima in Houston and bringing her back to Indonesia last Sunday to face drug trafficking charges.

"The awards are to honour their efforts, which I think are a remarkable success, in being able to arrest and bring Zarima back home for trial," Jakarta police chief Major-General Hamami Nata was quoted as saying during the presentation.
Indonesia and the United States have no extradition treaty, but Zarima, 24, agreed to return to Indonesia under police escort and in the company of her lawyer.
She was initially detained in August after police said they found pills of the designer drug in her home.
The actress, who has appeared in small roles in several local television serials, escaped shortly afterwards after asking if she could go home for a bath.
